title: Strings
subtitle: Runes and Ribbons
heading: ## Unit 9 ·

parts.scope: Lesson 8A "Strings Are Rows of Letters" (with 8A-remembers; all its exercises in order), Lesson 8B "Words That Change Shape" (with 8B-remembers; all its exercises in order, including any solo), and Quiz 8B
Extra practice 9X (8A-04, 8A-05, 8A-08, Quiz 8A), the optional Project 8P1 "The Water-Stained Log" (recommended) and the optional Project 8P2 "The Institute Cipher" (browser-only)
Quick Check 8 (both forms as testout items, plus their question forms as optional quiz items, the way Units 1-7 did) and the Strings cheatsheet

slips: calling a method and not keeping the result (line.lower() on its own line, then printing line unchanged) — methods hand back NEW strings, so reassign; lower(line) as if it were a function; trying to change a letter in place (word[0] = "T" → TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment); an index off by one, or a slice that misses its end; quotes inside quotes without an escape ("She said "hi"" → SyntaxError) and \n vs a typed newline; .split() hands back a LIST (then treating it as text); join called the wrong way round (words.join(" ") instead of " ".join(words)); int("7 ") or int("seven") without strip or a check; an f-string without the f (prints {name} literally) or with mismatched braces; + between text and a number without str(); .find() returning -1 read as the last position; case-sensitive `in` ("glow" in "Glow" is False); typing the finished text by hand instead of building it from the values.
earlierNote: Units 1-3 are shipped or in the open PR (in this folder from the repo). Units 4 (Lists), 5 (Dictionaries), 6 (Loops) and 7 (Functions II) are verified in staging and copied into this folder. Unit 8 (optional Code Challenges) introduces no new concepts and is not in this folder. This unit is INDEPENDENT of the Readiness Check (Unit 10 needs no Strings token); the teacher may run it before, alongside or after Module 2.
verifyNote: Fix every Unit 9 error until 0 errors (all earlier units' real files are in this folder, so run with concept_map.json moved aside first; if any error is only 'concept not introduced yet' for a token the plan gives a u08 prefix, restore the map and re-run with it, and report it).
extra: RPG tie-ins: Bomb Shell's clipped sentences (.split()), Lucky's "What's in it for me?" (methods), the greenroom sign "Greenroom, Interior" / "EXIT" (slicing), "It is NOT a compass" (.replace), Mar'tu's lines tidied with .lower().capitalize() (revisited from 6A-08), and the bars one more time. Mar'tu's framing: "Runes are only letters in a row. Python sees words the same way. Today we cut them, stretch them, and make them behave. Lucky, your notes are next." Objective 6: students must READ `+ str()` lines fluently because the campaign uses them, even though f-strings are taught too. Project 8P2 is browser-only until the teacher confirms IDLE. CONVENTIONS from the Unit 2 walkthrough fixes (read the repo's FORMAT.md): "Start like this" hints go LAST, never hint 1, and the last hint's line must be in the solution (the harness warns on both — leave none); solo items and Quick Check builders use explainer="lean"; Quick Check check messages name the slip and the evidence but never the fix; Quick Check forms set questions_to_pass like Unit 2's QC2. Honest tracing (Unit 3's ship): no Assemble rung that gives away a predicted/traced value; use the paste_stop setup guard on trace tasks. Never use worksheet-derived names or "Tester" in check data; invented Tor names only.
